answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Signed vintage car club membership with rally entries flips the bet — rallies entered under one name for years — and the sparrow lands on the attacker instead. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since rallies entered under one name for years takes calendar time as well as money — and the knoll is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the ridge of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
